accelera.def: To speed up; to make a car go faster than before.

accende.def: To switch on; to start an engine, a light or a phone.

aggiusto.def: To fix; to make a broken thing work again.

agosto.def: August; the hot month when half of Italy closes and leaves.

amicizia.def: Friendship; the bond between two people who like each other.

anguria.def: Watermelon; the huge green fruit that is red and wet inside.

animali.def: Animal; any living thing that is not a plant or a person.

anno.def: Year; the twelve months from January to December.

antipatica.def: Unpleasant; the kind of person nobody enjoys being with.

appuntamento.def: Appointment; a time agreed to meet a doctor or a friend.

armadio.def: Wardrobe; the tall cupboard where you hang your clothes.

arrabbiato.def: Angry; feeling bad with somebody for what they did.

aspirapolvere.def: Vacuum cleaner; the machine that sucks the dust off a floor.

autunno.def: Autumn; the months when the leaves fall and the air cools.

biancheria.def: Linen and underwear; the small washing you do by hand.

bici.def: Bike; the short everyday word Italians use for a bicycle.

biscotti.def: Biscuit; the small dry sweet Italians dip into their coffee.

bosco.def: Wood; a lot of trees growing together on a hillside.

bugie.def: Lie; something you say knowing it is not true.

busta.def: Envelope; the paper cover you keep letters or papers inside.

cacciavite.def: Screwdriver; the tool you turn to open or close a screw.

cassetto.def: Drawer; the box that slides out of a table or a cupboard.

chiave.def: Key; the small metal piece that opens a lock or a car.

clima.def: Climate; the kind of weather a place usually has.

colazione.def: Breakfast; the first food of the day, often coffee and biscuits.

coraggioso.def: Brave; able to act when other people are afraid.

cravatta.def: Tie; the long strip of cloth men knot around the collar.

discorso.def: Speech; the words somebody says in front of a crowd.

doccia.def: Shower; washing yourself standing up under falling water.

documenti.def: Document; an official paper with your name on it.

dolore.def: Pain; the bad feeling in a part of the body that hurts.

domenica.def: Sunday; the day when almost every Italian shop stays shut.

duro.def: Hard; not soft when you press it with your hand.

edificio.def: Building; any construction with walls and a roof.

educata.def: Polite; treating other people well even when they are difficult.

fattoria.def: Farm; the house and land where animals are kept.

fumo.def: Smoke; the grey cloud that rises from a fire.

funghi.def: Mushroom; the small round plant that grows in a wet wood.

gamberi.def: Prawn; the small pink sea animal you eat with the fingers.

gennaio.def: January; the first month of the year in Italy.

gettone.def: Token; the little metal piece you buy and give instead of money.

giovane.def: Young; with few years behind you, still near the start of life.

giugno.def: June; the month when the Italian school year finishes.

gola.def: Throat; the part inside your neck that hurts with a cold.

gonfia.def: Swollen; bigger than normal because it hurts inside.

graffio.def: Scratch; the thin line left on paint by something sharp.

grigia.def: Grey; the colour of a cloudy sky or of old metal.

insalata.def: Salad; raw green leaves with oil, salt and vinegar on top.

labbra.def: Lip; one of the two soft edges around your mouth.

lago.def: Lake; a large area of still water with land all around.

lampadina.def: Light bulb; the small glass ball that gives light in a lamp.

lasciato.def: To leave; to put a thing down and walk away from it.

lenti.def: Slow; taking a long time to move or to finish.

letti.def: Bed; the piece of furniture you lie down on to sleep.

maiale.def: Pork; the meat of the pig, and the animal itself.

malattia.def: Illness; the thing that keeps you in bed for some days.

male.def: Badly, and in fare male also to hurt or to be sore.

mamma.def: Mum; the warm everyday word Italians use for their mother.

mappa.def: Map; the drawing that shows roads and towns on paper.

marroni.def: Brown; the colour of wood, coffee or dry leaves.

marzo.def: March; the first month of spring in Italy.

materasso.def: Mattress; the thick soft part of a bed you lie on.

matrimonio.def: Wedding; the day two people marry and everybody eats a lot.

mattinata.def: Morning; here the whole stretch of hours before lunch.

melone.def: Melon; the sweet orange fruit Italians eat with ham.

mentito.def: To lie; to say something you know is not true.

mercoledì.def: Wednesday; the day in the middle of the working week.

mese.def: Month; one of the twelve parts a year is cut into.

messaggio.def: Message; the short text you send or get on a phone.

modulo.def: Form; the sheet with empty lines you have to fill in.

mucche.def: Cow; the big farm animal that gives milk every day.

multa.def: Fine; the money you pay when you break a traffic rule.

muovono.def: To move; to shift something from one place to another.

naso.def: Nose; the part of the face you breathe and smell with.

navi.def: Ship; the big boat that carries people and lorries across water.

nebbia.def: Fog; thick white air that stops you seeing far ahead.

notte.def: Night; the dark hours between the evening and the morning.

numerino.def: Queue ticket; the little paper with your number on it.

nuvola.def: Cloud; the white or grey shape that carries rain in the sky.

occhiali.def: Glasses; what you wear on your nose to see better.

orecchie.def: Ear; the part of the head you hear sounds with.

ottobre.def: October; the month when the weather turns cold in the hills.

palazzo.def: Large building; a block of flats or an old grand house.

panetteria.def: Bakery; the shop that sells bread fresh every morning.

panna.def: Cream; the thick white part of milk, sweet on a cake.

pantaloni.def: Trousers; the piece of clothing that covers both of your legs.

papà.def: Dad; the warm everyday word Italians use for their father.

parcheggia.def: To park; to leave the car standing in a free space.

parco.def: Park; the green public space with trees and benches.

passaporto.def: Passport; the small book you show to cross a border.

password.def: Password; the secret word you type to get onto a network.

pastiglie.def: Tablet; the small round medicine you swallow with water.

pastore.def: Shepherd; the person who walks all day behind a flock of sheep.

patate.def: Potato; the round vegetable that grows under the ground.

patente.def: Driving licence; the card that says you are allowed to drive.

paura.def: Fear; the cold feeling that something bad will happen.

pecore.def: Sheep; the white farm animal with thick soft wool.

pedaggio.def: Toll; the money you pay to use an Italian motorway.

pelle.def: Skin; the thin outside layer that covers your whole body.

peperoni.def: Pepper; the big red, yellow or green vegetable you roast.

persa.def: To get lost; to stop knowing where you are or which way to go.

petto.def: Chest; the front part of the body above the stomach.

pigiama.def: Pyjamas; the soft clothes you wear only in bed.

pneumatici.def: Tyre; the rubber ring on a wheel that touches the road.

pollo.def: Chicken; the meat of the bird that lives in a farmyard.

poltrona.def: Armchair; the soft wide seat for one person only.

pomata.def: Cream; the soft medicine you rub on a sore part of the body.

pomeriggio.def: Afternoon; the hours between lunch and the end of the day.

portatile.def: Laptop; the computer you can close and carry with you.

portiera.def: Car door; the door you open to get in or out.

posta.def: Post office; where letters and parcels are sent and picked up.

povera.def: Poor; with very little money for the things you need.

prenotazione.def: Booking; the room or table you asked for before arriving.

preoccupata.def: Worried; with a problem in your head that will not leave.

presa.def: Socket; the hole in the wall where you plug something in.

primavera.def: Spring; the months when the trees get their leaves back.

processione.def: Procession; people walking slowly together behind a holy statue.

prosciutto.def: Ham; the salted meat Italians cut in very thin slices.

pulita.def: Clean; with no dirt and no dust on it at all.

raccontava.def: To tell; to say a story to somebody from start to end.

rade.def: To shave; to cut the hair off your face with a blade.

raffreddore.def: Cold; the small illness with a blocked nose and a cough.

regala.def: To give as a present, without asking for money back.

relazione.def: Relationship; the way two people get on over the years.

ricca.def: Rich; with a lot of money and no worry about it.

ricevuta.def: Receipt; the paper that says you have paid for something.

rifugio.def: Mountain hut where walkers eat and sleep high up in the hills.

riposare.def: To rest; to stop working for a while and do nothing.

riposo.def: Rest; time with no driving and no work, so the body mends.

ritirare.def: To collect; to go and pick up something that is yours.

riunione.def: Meeting; when people at work sit together to decide things.

rompe.def: To break; to leave a thing in pieces or no longer working.

rubinetto.def: Tap; the metal part you turn to get water out.

sabato.def: Saturday; the day before Sunday, when Italian villages hold their feasts.

sagra.def: Village food festival; a few days of eating and music in the square.

salame.def: Salami; the dry sausage Italians cut in thin round slices.

salsa.def: Sauce; the wet part you pour over meat or over pasta.

salsicce.def: Sausage; the fat meat roll Italians cook over the coals.

sangue.def: Blood; the red liquid that runs inside the whole body.

santo.def: Saint; the holy person a village keeps a feast day for.

sapone.def: Soap; what you wash your hands and your body with.

scaffale.def: Shelf unit; the boards on a wall where books are kept.

scalda.def: To heat; to make food or a room warmer than before.

schermo.def: Screen; the flat glass part of a phone or a computer.

sciroppo.def: Syrup; the thick sweet medicine you take with a spoon.

scuola.def: School; the place where children go to learn every morning.

scura.def: Dark; with little light, or close to black in colour.

secca.def: Dry; with no water in it, said of air or of clothes.

secchio.def: Bucket; the round container you carry water in.

seguire.def: To follow; to go behind somebody or along a line.

semaforo.def: Traffic light; the red, yellow and green light at a crossing.

sentiero.def: Path; the narrow way through a wood or up a hill.

settembre.def: September; the month when Italian holidays end and work restarts.

soggiorno.def: Living room; the room with the sofa where people sit together.

sogni.def: Dream; the story your head tells you while you sleep.

soluzione.def: Solution; the way out of a problem you have found.

sorella.def: Sister; the daughter of your own mother and father.

sorprende.def: To surprise; to do something nobody was expecting from you.

spaventa.def: To frighten; to make somebody feel afraid of something.

spazzolino.def: Toothbrush; the small brush you clean your teeth with.

specchio.def: Mirror; the glass where you see your own face.

spedita.def: To post; to send a letter or a parcel through the post office.

sporca.def: Dirty; covered with dust, mud or something you want to clean.

sportello.def: Counter window; the small opening where an office serves you.

spugna.def: Sponge; the soft thing you wash or clean a surface with.

spuntino.def: Snack; a small quick thing to eat between two meals.

stanchezza.def: Tiredness; the heavy feeling after too many hours awake.

stipendio.def: Salary; the money that arrives every month from a job.

stivali.def: Boot; the tall shoe that covers part of your leg.

storia.def: Story, and also history; Italian uses the same word for both.

studentessa.def: Female student; a young woman who studies at school or university.

stupida.def: Stupid; feeling foolish about something you said or thought.

suda.def: To sweat; what your skin does when you are too hot.

supermercato.def: Supermarket; the big shop with all the food on shelves.

sveglia.def: To wake up; to open your eyes and stop sleeping.

tamburo.def: Drum; the round instrument you hit to keep the beat.

tapparella.def: Roller blind; the shutter you pull down over an Italian window.

tappeto.def: Rug or carpet; the cloth on the floor you walk on.

targa.def: Number plate; the metal plate with the letters of a car.

tasti.def: Key or button; the small part you press on a keyboard.

telefonata.def: Phone call; the moment you ring somebody and talk.

temperatura.def: Temperature; how hot or how cold the air or a body is.

termometro.def: Thermometer; the small tool that tells you how high a fever is.

timbro.def: Stamp; the ink mark an office puts on a paper to make it valid.

topo.def: Mouse; the small grey animal that runs into a hole.

torcia.def: Torch; the small lamp you carry to see in the dark.

torta.def: Cake; the sweet you cut in slices for the whole table.

tristezza.def: Sadness; the low quiet feeling after something goes wrong.

trombe.def: Trumpet; the loud metal instrument you blow into.

tè.def: Tea; the hot drink you make with leaves and hot water.

uccello.def: Bird; the animal with feathers that sings and flies.

umida.def: Damp; with water in the air or on a surface.

uva.def: Grapes; the small sweet fruit that grows in bunches.

vacanze.def: Holiday; the days you stop working and go somewhere else.

venerdì.def: Friday; the last day of the Italian working week.

verbale.def: Written report; the page where damage is listed and signed.

verità.def: Truth; what really happened, said without changing it.

vernice.def: Paint; the coloured layer on the outside of a car or a wall.

veste.def: To get dressed; to put your clothes on before going out.

viaggia.def: To travel; to go from one place to a far one.

vinto.def: To win; to come first or to get what you were fighting for.

visto.def: To see; to notice something with your eyes.
